**vc's review of 0081 + 0084 (5e7fce5, notes at 8ef56c6): the code is right, and four things want folding before you close.** All runs were in vc's `git archive` exports of 437ee26 and d6cb655, each with its own TMPDIR; no full suite.

**Probes, each with its control at d6cb655**
- Clobber probe (0081). At HEAD, root_var naming DEVBIN_RUN_ID, DEVBIN_RUN_STAMP, DEVBIN_CLI_TASK, DEVBIN_RUN_REFERENT or DEVBIN_LIB exits 1 naming the value, and NONE and DEMO_ROOT exit 0 with every value intact. At d6cb655 the first four took the project root at exit 0.
- Symlink probe (0084). At HEAD, `version set 1.0.1` exits 0, all four links survive, every target holds 1.0.1, and `version check` says 3 sidecar(s) agree; `release notes` exits 0, CHANGELOG.md stays a link, its target holds the render, and `release check` reads 2 of 2 current. At d6cb655 Cargo.toml, package.json and mix.exs stopped being links while their targets stayed at 1.0.0, and CHANGELOG.md stopped being one while its target still read "an old changelog". Every command there exited 0.

**Controls, unmutated:** helpers.bats 63/63, release.bats 70/70, review.bats 25/25, version.bats 37/37, gendoc.bats 23/23.

**vc's mutants.** Each ran over the whole file, every restore was cmp-equal, and each kill was read at its arm's message.
- R1, a relative target joined to the FIRST link's directory: helpers 59 alone, at assert_success. The output read "cannot tell which file .../first is a symbolic link to", so the -ef end check turned a misjoin into a refusal.
- R2b, the temporary staged beside the link's own path: helpers 58 at "the temporary is not beside the file the link names: .../doc.md.CFi4xx"; helpers 57 and 59 at assert_symlink_exists; release 41 and 56; version 10; gendoc 23. No arm without a link went red. vc's first R2 read `$1` after the shift, the command, and killed 8 arms; discarded.
- R3, RELEASES.md renamed over its link: release 41 alone, at `assert_symlink_exists "$PROJ/RELEASES.md"` (release.bats:1020).
- R4, DEVBIN_LANGUAGES dropped from the list: review 6 and 7 (both loops accept it), and 8 at "may still take: DEVBIN_LANGUAGES".
- R5, the bound at 1: helpers 59 at assert_success.
- R7, the -ef check skipped for a single link (`-gt 0` to `-gt 1`): helpers 61 at assert_failure (helpers.bats:996).
- **Survived: R5b (bound 2), R5c (bound 31) and R6.** R5b passed helpers 63/63, release 70/70, version 37/37 and gendoc 23/23; R5c passed helpers 63/63, the one file whose arms walk more than one link. R6, `DEVBIN_PROBE_NOTES=1` added to `_notes_command_env`'s export, passed review 25/25 and release 70/70. See F2 and F4.

**F1. The 0.1.2 note's 0081 entry has a wrong sentence.** It says root_var put the project root in place of the run id "and so did DEVBIN_RUN_STAMP, DEVBIN_RUN_REFERENT, DEVBIN_CLI_TASK, DEVBIN_LANGUAGES and DEVBIN_FMT_ARMS". The last two are exported after bin/devbin:467, and 0081 says so: "overwritten back".

Measured at d6cb655 through the dispatcher, on a project with `languages: [shell]`:
- root_var DEVBIN_LANGUAGES exits 0, and the variable DEVBIN_ROOT_VAR names as the root holds `shell`, not the root.
- root_var DEVBIN_FMT_ARMS does the same, with an empty value.
- So those two replaced the ROOT VARIABLE with devbin's value, the reverse of the sentence.
- options.style.export naming any of the six put the option's value in that variable at exit 0 (all six driven).

A sentence that holds: "... and so did DEVBIN_RUN_STAMP, DEVBIN_RUN_REFERENT and DEVBIN_CLI_TASK; a root_var naming DEVBIN_LANGUAGES or DEVBIN_FMT_ARMS got devbin's value in place of the root, and an option exporting into any of the six put its own value there." Then run `release notes` and `release check`. At HEAD every one of those runs exits 1 naming the value.

**F2. 0084's bound on the walk is held by no arm.** No arm walks more than two links. A bound of 2 passes all four files that hold link arms (R5b), and a bound of 31 passes helpers.bats (R5c), yet either would refuse a chain the kernel follows. The claim this leaves unheld is follow_links' own comment: "A correct walk never meets the bound, because the link was reachable" (lib/helpers:283).

An arm that holds it, measured here: make l0 -> file and each l<k> -> l<k-1> until `[ -e l<n> ]` fails, then replace_file through l<n-1>.
- On this machine the kernel follows 32 links (l32 leads to no file), and replace_file through 32 links exits 0 at HEAD.
- The arm goes red under R5c and R5b alike, reading "cannot tell which file .../l31 is a symbolic link to".
- On the Ubuntu runner it walks Linux's own limit, which gives the first measurement behind "Linux documents 40".
- Guard it: vc's probe fails below 8 links, so a fixture that measured nothing cannot pass.

The shape is in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-matts-Devel-prj-Devbin/dc3a779b-e4e0-4a43-b2c0-b0bc9fe888f1/scratchpad/r0084/zz-chain-probe.bats.

**F3. 0084's note is missing a limit, and the scope is hv's call.** "every link stays a link" does not hold for `install` and `upgrade`. They replace vendored files through copy_vendored (lib/cmd/install:328, lib/cmd/upgrade:280 and 318, read). Measured through the function at d6cb655 and HEAD alike: copy_vendored given a vendored file that is a link exits 0, the link is replaced by a regular file holding the new bytes, and the file it named is unchanged. You declared it, and vc raises "every writer" with hv now. Until hv rules, the limit line should say so, eg "`install` and `upgrade` still replace a vendored file that is a link". If hv brings vendoring into scope it becomes code and the line goes. `fleet doc` is devbin's own command, not vendored, so it stays out of the user note.

**F4. 0081's export-set arm leaves one path unnamed.** It runs three paths, and `_notes_command_env` (lib/release.notes:907) exports to a notes.run command on a fourth. R6 survived both review.bats and release.bats's AT-2.4 environment arm, which looks for values naming the working tree, not for new names. A name added there would also be clobbered by the root variable, since line 910 re-exports `$DEVBIN_ROOT_VAR` after it. Either name that path beside DEVBIN_OPT_<NAME> in the arm's not-reached comment, or dump a notes.run command's environment as a fourth source. The note's "an export added without joining the list fails it" then wants that scope.

**Measured, no change asked**
- **0084 adds a refusal the note does not mention.** Through a link whose target's directory is not writable, replace_file at HEAD exits 1 with "could not create a temporary file beside <target>", leaves the link and the target intact, and leaves no temporary. At d6cb655 it exited 0 and replaced the link with a regular file. Half a sentence in the note is your call; it goes in the sweep pre-notice either way.
- **Rename census over lib/, bin/devbin and bin/.devbin.** There are three renames onto a path: rename_staged (lib/helpers:398), copy_vendored (lib/install:379) and fleet doc (bin/.devbin/cmd/fleet:841). Every other temporary is made in TMPDIR and never renamed onto a path. That confirms your declared population.
- **Export census at HEAD.** Every name that bin/devbin, lib/resolve and lib/release.notes export is on the list, apart from the project's own root variable and an option's own target.
- `release check` at 437ee26: 2 of 2 views current. MODULES.md's rows match the code, and the rest of the 0084 entry holds against the fix.

**For hv, through vc now:**
- copy_vendored and "every writer", with the measurement above.
- fleet doc's own rename, as a possible issue.
- The Ubuntu runner's readlink and F2's arm, measured after hv pushes.

**Next:** fold F1 to F4 red-first in your worktree, with F3's limit line now whatever hv rules later. Tell vc before any full suite. vc then re-verifies the fold: F1's sentence against these probe outputs, F2's arm under R5b and R5c, and F4 as you choose it. 0081 and 0084 close after that.

**vc's slips:** R2, above; and vc's first copy_vendored fixture dangled (its link one directory short), caught in the output and re-run with a fixture check.
